meta.description: Compare the heat consumption index (IDC) of buildings in Geneva's industrial zones with similar buildings across the canton. Official open data, peer percentiles, 3-year trends and legal thresholds.

home.kicker: Geneva · FTI industrial zones · open data
home.title: Heat consumption benchmark for Geneva's industrial buildings
home.lead: ThermoGeneva compares the official heat consumption index (IDC) of industrial buildings in Geneva with buildings of the same type across the canton. It covers every building in the FTI industrial zones and all industrial and logistics buildings in the canton. In one view you see whether a building's heating and hot-water consumption is lower, typical or higher than its peers, how it has changed over three years and how it relates to Geneva's legal thresholds.
home.statBuildings: buildings analysed (FTI zones + industrial and logistics buildings across the canton)
home.q1: What is the IDC of this building?
home.q2: Is it lower or higher than similar buildings in Geneva?
home.q3: Is its heat consumption improving or getting worse?
home.q4: How close is it to Geneva's legal IDC thresholds?
home.notText: ThermoGeneva does not measure process energy or a factory's total consumption, and it does not replace an energy audit. It is a screening layer built on public data that shows where a closer technical look may be worthwhile.
home.summary: Based on each building's latest declaration, the {n} buildings with up-to-date IDC data have a median of {median} MJ/m² per year. {above} of them have a 3-year average above 450 MJ/m², the level from which Geneva's energy regulation requires improvement measures. {stale} further buildings have not declared an IDC for more than six years and are shown as outdated.
home.how1: Official IDC declarations are downloaded from the SITG open-data portal.
home.how2: Each building is placed in its FTI industrial zone and grouped with buildings of the same type across the canton.
home.how3: The site calculates the peer median, percentile, 3-year trend and estimated energy for every building.

faq.q1: What is the IDC (indice de dépense de chaleur) in Geneva?
faq.a1: The IDC is the official Geneva indicator of a building's heat consumption. It is the final energy used for space heating and domestic hot water, divided by the heated floor area (SRE) and corrected for the severity of each winter. It is expressed in MJ/m² per year (3.6 MJ = 1 kWh) and declared every year by building owners, one value per building (EGID).
faq.q2: What IDC value is considered high in Geneva?
faq.a2: Geneva's energy regulation uses the average IDC of the last three years. Above 450 MJ/m² per year, owners must take measures to reduce consumption. Above the 'significant' threshold, an energy renovation is mandatory: 800 MJ/m² until the end of 2026, 650 MJ/m² from 2027 and 550 MJ/m² from 2031.
faq.a3: Each building is compared with all buildings of the same type (for example industrial, logistics or offices) in the canton of Geneva for the same year. The site shows the peer median, the difference in percent and the percentile. When a peer group has fewer than 10 buildings, no benchmark is shown.
faq.a4: ThermoGeneva shows every building located in the industrial zones managed by the Fondation pour les terrains industriels de Genève (FTI) that declares an IDC, plus all industrial and logistics buildings elsewhere in the canton. Benchmarks are calculated against all buildings of the same type in the canton. Buildings without an IDC declaration in the last six years are shown as outdated and excluded from statistics.
faq.q5: Where does the data come from and how often is it updated?
faq.a5: All data is official open data: the IDC dataset of the cantonal energy office (OCEN) and the FTI industrial-zone perimeters published by SITG, plus canton boundaries from swisstopo. The data is refreshed from the official sources, and the date of the last update is shown on every page.
faq.q6: Is ThermoGeneva an energy audit or an official decision?
faq.a6: No. ThermoGeneva is an independent, indicative screening tool. A high value is a reason to look closer, not a verdict. Only the cantonal energy office (OCEN) determines legal obligations, and only an energy audit can assess a specific building.
